Define G1-derived windows from a fragment file

Source: R/g1_windows.R
define_G1_windows.Rd

Build variable-width genomic windows that each hold target_reads G1 fragments, and count fragments of all cells in those windows.

Usage

define_G1_windows(
  genome_granges,
  frag_path,
  meta_data,
  g1_col = "is_G1",
  cov_col = "coverage",
  target_reads = 200,
  target_window_length = 20000,
  min.gapwidth = 100000L,
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

genome_granges

A GRanges of retained genome bins (already filtered for gaps / CNV / mappability, e.g. the output of filter_windows(), unlisted, or of synchronize_bins()).

frag_path

Path to a bgzipped, tabix-indexed 10x fragment file (<frag_path>.tbi must exist). Columns: chr, start (0-based), end, barcode, ...

meta_data

A data.frame whose unique row names are cell barcodes.

g1_col

Column of meta_data flagging G1 cells (coerced to logical).

cov_col

Numeric column of meta_data with per-cell coverage.

target_reads

Positive integer; G1 fragments per window. We use 200.

target_window_length

Positive integer; target median window length (bp) and minimum contig width, e.g. 20000.

min.gapwidth

Positive integer passed to GenomicRanges::reduce(). Default 100000L.

verbose

Logical; report progress. Default FALSE.

Value

A list with

g1bins_counts

dgCMatrix windows x cells (column names = rownames(meta_data), row names = window IDs "<chr>-<start>-<end>").

g1bins

named GRanges of windows with metadata columns midpoint, g1_read_count, is_masked_window (G1 count differs from target_reads by more than 1) and contig_id. Its S4Vectors::metadata() holds target_reads, target_window_length, pilot_chr, selected_g1_n, selected_g1_barcodes, selected_cov_cutoff, pilot_median_length, pilot_n_windows.

Details

Steps:

  1. genome_granges is merged with GenomicRanges::reduce(min.gapwidth) into contigs; contigs shorter than target_window_length and contigs on chromosomes absent from the tabix index are dropped.

  2. G1 cells (meta_data[[g1_col]] is TRUE, finite coverage) are ranked by decreasing coverage.

  3. On a pilot chromosome (largest total contig width), a binary search chooses the number n of top-ranked G1 cells whose windows have a median length closest to target_window_length.

  4. For every chromosome, fragment midpoints (((start0 + 1) + end) %/% 2) of the n selected G1 cells are sorted per contig and cut into consecutive blocks of target_reads; each window runs from the first fragment of its block to just before the first fragment of the next block (the last block ends at its last fragment; the incomplete remainder is dropped). If a chromosome has >= 100 windows, windows outside the 1st-99th length percentiles are removed.

  5. Fragments of all cells in rownames(meta_data) are counted per window (by midpoint).
